This ride is a social ride, but cyclists are not expected to stay in one group. Cyclists may pedal at their own comfortable paces. Please be supportive of the other cyclists to avoid anyone biking alone or being dropped off the back of the last group.

item.title: Inspiration! at The Barn at Paradise Station — Fri Oct 23, 7:30 PM — The Barn at Paradise Station
item.description:
What’s your Inspiration? Join our stunning vocal trio, Perfect Harmony, as we take you on a musical journey of inspiring songs from Folk to Film, Broadway to Gospel and our favorite Sacred music that stands the test of time. Featuring professional vocalists from Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, a live band, beautiful costumes and more of the original and inspiring arrangements Perfect Harmony is known for, you are sure to love this trip down memory lane. Perfect Harmony has toured across the Mid-Atlantic region to locations like The White House, The Billy Graham Library in Charlotte, NC; Dollywood Theme Park in Pigeon Forge, TN; The Great Auditorium in Ocean Grove, NJ and the Ohio Star Theater in Sugarcreek, OH. They have also opened for Larry Gatlin of Gatlin Brothers fame.

item.title: Valley Forge Park River Trail (Pawlings Rd) — Sun Oct 25, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Walking Tails Directions: From the intersection of Egypt Road and Park Ave./Pawlings Road, proceed on Pawlings Road heading towards the Schuylkill River. You will pass Mill Grove on your right, St. Gabriel Hall on your left and Pawling Farm on your left. You are getting close when you pass Sullivan Blvd. on your left and Gertrude St. on your right. You turn left on the next and last left (right before you go over the bridge over the Schuylkill River). Look for the River Trail Valley Forge Park sign visible from Pawlings Road. The gravel parking lot is straight ahead and also visible from Pawlings Road. If you go over the bridge over the Schuylkill River, you have gone too far and are now in Chester county.
CLICK DIRECTLY ON THE MAP IF YOU THINK YOU ARE LOST. IT WILL BRING YOU RIGHT TO US WHERE WE MEET.
This walk goes out about 1.5 miles along the Schuylkill River and then we come back the way we came, for a total of 3 miles. This is a dirt/gravel/mulch trail through the woods.

item.title: Contemplative Citizenship — Tue Oct 27, 7:00 PM — Saint James Chapel and Zoom
item.description:
Contemplative Citizenship: Lord, make me an instrument of your peace. October 13 – November 10 7 – 8:00 PM in the Chapel In person and via Zoom This Fall, our worship and teaching will be guided by a single line from the Prayer of Saint Francis: “Lord, make me an instrument of your peace.” We will begin this initiative at our Saturday Night Mass on October 3, with local musician and pastor Liz Fulmer leading music that inspires us to embody God’s peace in our lives. On Tuesday, October 13, we will start a 5-week Fall Contemplative Citizenship series in which we will reflect on various lines from the prayer, exploring what it means to embody this prayer in both our personal lives and in our civic responsibilities, especially during this election season when our country feels divided and stressed.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Evening Compline — Tue Oct 27, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.description:
What’s your go-to fireside story? What about that family tale that’s so extraordinary that it’s unbelievable? In this workshop, we’ll hone our narrative craft (including setting, character, and description) as we flesh out the stories we grew up hearing, telling, and passing along! Students in this course will read and respond to a sample text, draft their own heirloom story, and receive feedback from peers and instructor. While there won’t be a literal campfire, we’ll spend the evening spinning yarns. After all, everyone’s got a story to tell! This is a lecture based and creative writing class with some lecture and guidance followed by time to write using the skills learned in class.

item.title: Evening Compline — Mon Oct 26, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster
